title: The Spear Hero and the Heroes’ Council [Part 2]
text: “W-well then… let’s talk about swapping members between the Spear Hero and the Bow Hero.”

My fiancée is forcefully steering the conversation toward me and Itsuki. She’s been acting all nervous for a while now. After all, both Ren and Itsuki—who are Heroes—are terrifying when they get really angry. Plus, now that my Father has heard that his Assistant was killed, he’s furious just like he was back when it happened to Kou—any ordinary person would be terrified.
Huh? Itsuki is glaring at me with a terrifying expression. Well… Itsuki and I have clashed repeatedly during this loop, so I suppose it’s only natural that he’d look like that.
“Motoyasu, what do you take my comrades for?! I’m not talking about Ren-san, but I heard you were dragging them around in a high-and-mighty, forceful manner.”
“They were trying to ambush others and raid hunting grounds, and since they didn’t like it, they tried to stage a boycott.”
“Even so, what’s with paralyzing them and dragging them along with a rope?!”
“Just like you, I made sure to level them up sufficiently. They’re weak anyway. I think they had plenty of healing Magic.”
“What’s that supposed to mean! Naofumi! Aren’t you going to tell Motoyasu off?!”
Ren spoke up, as if to protest, addressing my father. My father looked troubled. It seems I’ve put him in a difficult position because of me. I’m sorry, Father.
“Well… it’s Motoyasu… If there was anything I could do about it, I would’ve done it already…”
With a distant look in his eyes, my father averted his gaze.
“Ah… right, that’s true. Motoyasu was that kind of guy.”
Ren’s earlier murderous intent had vanished, and he’d calmed down. Why was he satisfied with that explanation? Anyway, let’s continue.
“Honestly, is Itsuki planning to start a religion or something? Itsuki’s friends tried to force me to address him as ‘Itsuki-sama.’”
“What? Is that true?”
“It’s no lie. If you want, you should swap members with Itsuki’s group.”
“Hmm…”
Ren is staring intently at Itsuki. Perhaps sensing that his gaze was making things awkward, Itsuki hurriedly spoke up.
“That’s not all! Motoyasu-san, your companions… were they Filolials, right? What are they all about! They all ganged up on me and bombarded me with questions!”
It seems Itsuki is feeling a bit embarrassed too, as he’s trying to change the subject. Even if he says that, I’ll just calmly state the facts.
“It’s because you wouldn’t answer honestly. I suppose Yuki-chan and the others’ intellectual curiosity got the better of them.”
“Oh, that…”
“What happened?”
“When I got here, they were surrounding Itsuki with Motoyasu-kun, chanting ‘Why? Why?’ over and over… It was a little creepy, maybe.”
“Whoa… If that’s the kind of owner, then that’s the kind of monster.”

Is it just my imagination, or is some strange sense of trust forming between Ren and my Father? Fine. If sacrificing me can help Motoyasu, my Father, and Ren build a friendship, then I’ll gladly bear the stigma.

“They’re not really that kind of kids, though… Just as they look, they’re still kids. That’s probably why they questioned Itsuki’s actions. You know how kids ask adults ‘why, why?’ all the time? It’s just like that.”
“Even so, they blocked my attacks and got in my way, and they just assumed I was holding back—they wouldn’t even let me defend myself!”
“I asked about that too, and I think Yuki pointed out some solid evidence, didn’t she?　Why didn’t you answer her?”
That’s obvious. You must have had something to hide, which is why you couldn’t answer honestly.
“What are you talking about?”
“According to Yuki-chan, you weren’t pulling the bowstring back at all. Plus, she said you were waiting for your teammates to get into trouble. Apparently, you always attacked one step too late.”
“…I see. If that’s true, it’s a problem.”
“It’s a bit much to just believe one side of the story, so if there was a reason, tell me. If you tell me now, I’ll explain it to Yuki and the others myself.”
“You were fighting just a moment ago—what are you two suddenly getting along about?!”

Rin was startled by Itsuki’s remark and glared at Father. But at the same time, she frowned at Itsuki. Still, she hasn’t answered Father’s question. He’s planning to brush it off and gloss over it, isn’t he?
“That’s a separate issue. So? Were you just waiting for your friend to be in trouble?”
“Itsuki loves justice, so he was waiting for the perfect moment to come to the rescue in a cool way.”

Since this is knowledge from the future, I’m definitely right about this. The same problem was pointed out during the meeting in the first world, too. By Filo-tan! Plus, I heard that my Big Sister was angry about it, so it’s deeply etched into my brain.
“Well, if you pulled a stunt like that, of course she’d want to know. And on top of that, knowing you, you were even lying, weren’t you?”
“When did I ever lie?!”
“I heard it through the grapevine. That You, Itsuki, are hiding your true identity while carrying out your ‘social reform’ in a way that’s as obvious as day. That part’s already a lie, isn’t it?”
“That’s a completely different matter!”
“You’re trying to use your allies as human shields.”
“I see. Purely in terms of efficiency, it’s not a bad move, but I wouldn’t want you on my side.”
That’s a massive boomerang! You’re completely ignoring your own behavior. You should have that stalker pig throw a projectile at you. It might clear up those brain cells that seem to be brainwashed.
“Give it a rest already! Right now, this is a discussion between me and Motoyasu.”
“Then how about we swap out Itsuki’s and my team members starting tomorrow? That way, we’ll see whether Itsuki or Motoyasu is right.”
“O-okay. I’ll make the necessary arrangements.”
His Finacée seemed to sense that they’d reached an agreement and said that. It looks like the team swap will continue with just Itsuki and Ren.
“Guh…”
“Not that again. How many times are you going to whine about this?”

Itsuki glared at me sharply. I hope I can successfully hide my true identity during the training. Well, knowing Itsuki, he’s probably already given all sorts of orders to his so-called “comrades”—who are really just a bunch of religious fanatics. But will he be able to give specific instructions on what to do? He might be able to cover up his lies, but it’ll be interesting to see if he can fool his “comrades.”
“Bow Hero, Spear Hero, have you two finished your discussion? I’d like to move on to the next agenda item.”
“No problem.”
“…There are various things I’d like to say, but I’ll hold off for now.”

Even though I have my thoughts, I’ll hold back. That’s how eager Itsuki and the others are to learn the methods of strengthening. It’s a slightly unsettling situation, but it’s essential if we’re to overcome what lies ahead.
“Well then, let’s begin the main topic: the exchange of information among the Heroes.”

My Finacée made the announcement. Ren and Itsuki fell silent at that point. Most likely, they’re thinking about how to pry out the secrets of the strength that I and my Father are hiding. In the first world, they wouldn’t believe us, but now—starting with Yuki-chan and seeing how strong my Assistants are—they might just believe us.

And the moment the topic of information exchange came up, Ren and Itsuki fell silent. It was almost eerie. It was as if the commotion from earlier had never happened. It’s certain that neither Ren nor Itsuki wants to explain the enhancement methods they know.

I’d been thinking it might be best for me to keep quiet, too. I didn’t think there was any need to confirm the enhancement methods I already knew, and I certainly didn’t feel any obligation to teach them to someone who didn’t know them anyway.

But I remember that back then, Father’s persuasive skills left me with no choice but to speak up. I figured if I didn’t, I’d be branded a troublesome troublemaker who lacked team spirit and get pushed aside by the other three. I, Motoyasu, must commend Father’s persuasive skills.
“…Naofumi-san. Why don’t you go first?”
Itsuki broke the silence and said to Father. I’ve heard that line before.
“Well… I guess there’s no need to hide it. I haven’t been told directly by those two, but I’ve learned their strengthening methods indirectly from Motoyasu-kun, after all.”
“I’m not hiding anything!”

Itsuki has a short fuse, doesn’t he? Ren is also glaring at my Father with a look of displeasure. So when I fixed Ren with an intense stare, he turned away, looking somewhat pale. Should I try closing one eye for effect?
“Ugh…”
Ren groaned, covering his mouth with his hand. What exactly is bothering him?
“You two… were you in that kind of relationship?”
“What!?”
My father said this, looking back and forth between Ren and me. Isn’t he misunderstanding something?
“Hmph. It’s common knowledge that Itsuki has a habit of keeping secrets. There’s no room for doubt.”
“Is it really that fun to pick on me?! I’m speechless—and to think you’re supposed to be a hero!”
Hearing Ren’s words, Itsuki is about to start arguing again. They really never learn, do they?
“Now, now. I’ve heard everything from Motoyasu-kun, so I’m not going to keep quiet. I already know about the methods for strengthening Ren and Itsuki, too.”
“What kind of nonsense are you—”
“For now, I want you to listen on the assumption that what Ren, Itsuki, and Motoyasu-kun said—that they came from the future of this world—is true.”
“Oh, you mean the one where Naofumi gets a bird girl? And the part where he sleeps with a guy and has a kid?”

“W-well, that’s just because Motoyasu-kun’s explanation was really bad—but the part about coming from the future is true. That’s why he knows so much about the country’s secrets and how to enhance the Hero’s weapons. We’ve even already put the methods for strengthening Ren and Itsuki into practice.”
My father is desperately explaining the situation to Ren and Itsuki. He told them nothing but the unvarnished truth, without holding anything back. But…

“I can’t believe it. Most likely, Motoyasu himself must have been eavesdropping on the castle folk’s conversations when he left his room on the night he was summoned, right? Maybe he stumbled upon a secret meeting between the king and the princess or something.”

“That’s entirely possible. He probably used Naofumi, with his weak class, to navigate the situation after learning of the conspiracy. It wasn’t Itsuki, but he must have found a good cover to blend in.”

What?! So they found out I went out at night? Well, since I went to the Filolial House, I suppose everyone knows about that anyway. It seems no one has figured out that I killed the Smoked Meat back then, though. I’ll have to be more careful the next time I carry out an assassination. Though, killing the Smoked Meat was completely pointless, so I doubt I’ll do it again.

“...Moving on, the proof is that Motoyasu was very strong and knew a lot of things. Right from the first day, he could use the Portal skill and get to Siltvelt in an instant. Thanks to that, I was able to get stronger without the country noticing.”
“It’s obvious that Motoyasu-san is strong because he’s cheating! Knowledge from the future? Then why didn’t you stop me from being used!”
“Because I thought you wouldn’t believe me even if I told you. In fact, I told you many times. Back then, did you believe what I said, Itsuki?”
“Judging by the results alone, Itsuki didn’t believe what Motoyasu-kun said.”
“Ugh…”
You know exactly what I’m talking about, don’t you? Well, I did say it over and over. It’s Itsuki’s fault for not listening to me or my Father before the damage got worse.
“I don’t mean to blame you for that, though. It would’ve been crazy to take a story about someone coming from the future at face value back then.”

Hmm, Father is certainly right—it’s hard to get anyone to believe something as outlandish as “I came from the future.” In fact, even in Father’s case, he gained my trust by reaching out to him when he was still hurting after being falsely accused. I suspect that right after I rescued him from that false accusation, Father was listening to me with a mix of skepticism and belief.
